subject: FinWise load test coordination — SLOs, k6 script, and test window
messages:
From: Trevor Mills <trevor.mills@finwise.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, logan_wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinWise Performance Team <perf-team@finwise.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: load test coordination for Redwood integration

Hi Marissa / Logan —

Thanks again for the demo today. We want to run a customer-led load test against the Redwood integration next week to validate end-to-end latency and concurrency behavior before ramp. Key SLOs and asks: 

- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for non-streaming generation; for streaming responses we expect initial token latency <= 150ms and steady-state token emission 20-30ms/token.
- Throughput: target sustained 200 requests/sec (each request ~1.5k tokens).
- Concurrency: up to 50 concurrent user sessions, with spike tests to 80 for short bursts.
- Streaming: we need full stream support (chunked token delivery) — confirm keep-alive & SSE support for the test.

We plan to run the test window: Wed 21 Apr 2027 10:00–12:00 PT. We'll execute from our CI (k6) and can provide the script if helpful.

What we need from Redwood before the run:
- Test API key / test account + endpoint to hit (non-prod sandbox that mirrors prod latency).
- IP allowlist ranges for our CI egress so we can open firewall rules.
- Any recommended k6 config (ramp-up, vus, thresholds) and a runbook/checklist for the test.

Happy to coordinate a 15-min pre-test sync early next week. Who should be on standby during the run?

Thanks,
Trevor
Trevor Mills
Dir. Performance Engineering, FinWise

- p95 <= 250ms non-streaming; streaming initial latency <= 150ms; token emission 20–30ms/token.
- Sustained 200 rps (1.5k token payload avg), concurrency 50, spike to 80.
- Streaming support confirmed; we'll validate SSE/HTTP chunked behavior during the pre-test sync.
- Test window proposed: Wed 21 Apr 10:00–12:00 PT.

What Redwood will provide (owners):
- Test account + API key (marissa) — I will provision a sandbox account and post the invite link in a secure doc by Mon 19 Apr.
- Egress IP ranges for allowlist (logan) — see attachment with current egress ranges; confirm with your infra team.
- k6 template & recommended params (attached) — I’ve attached redwood-k6-template.js as a starting point.
- On-call support during the run (rishi) — rishi will be our test lead/ops contact for the window.

Action items / timeline: 
1) Marissa: provision test account + post secure invite (by Mon 19 Apr).
2) Trevor: confirm your egress IPs and share k6 script (you mentioned you have one).
3) Logan: confirm allowlist ranges and any TLS/fingerprint requirements.
4) Team sync: 15-min pre-test check Mon 19 Apr 11:00 PT (please confirm).

Attachments: redwood-k6-template.js (application/javascript) — basic scenario, ramp, and streaming validation check.

Let me know if the window or any targets need adjustment. We’ll plan for the 21 Apr slot pending the pre-test sync.

—Marissa

Hi Trevor —

Thanks for the IP list — those addresses look good. A few notes from the infra side: 

- Confirmed allowlist: 34.120.45.22/32, 34.120.45.23/32, 34.120.45.24/32. I’ve attached our current egress ranges for reference (redwood-egress-ip-ranges.txt) — if your CI runs from additional ranges let us know ASAP.
- API key headers: use Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>. We’ll provision a sandbox key with a narrow policy for the run.
- k6 recommendations: ramp-up 5 min to target vus, steady 90 min, thresholds on p95 < 250ms and error rate < 0.5%. For streaming checks set shorter iteration timeouts and validate chunk boundaries.
- Keep-alive: ensure HTTP/1.1 keep-alive and socket pool config in k6 to avoid connection churn.

I’ll send the allowlist confirmation to our access team once Marissa posts the test account.

—Logan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — I’ll be on-call for the run and will join the pre-test sync on Mon 19 Apr 11:00 PT. Quick checklist/runbook for the run (short):

- Pre-run: verify sandbox key (scope: test-only), validate allowlist, confirm endpoint URL and health check returns 200.
- Warmup: 10–15 min ramp to 50% target traffic to populate caches/KV.
- Main run: steady-state at 200 rps for 60–90 min, with 3x 2-min spike tests to 80 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming validation: run a short streaming scenario after steady state to confirm chunk latency (collect sample traces).
- Post-run: collect request traces, token-level timing, and the k6 results archive.

Slack/contact: I’ll be on #cust-finwise-loadtests (invite will be shared) and reachable at rishi@redwood.ai and +1 (415) 555-0239 during the window. I’ll also publish the runbook link in the pre-test sync invite.

Looking forward — see you on Mon for the checklist.

—Rishi
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
